[2026-07-28 06:39] FLEX-001 x8 added to precision batch: flags containers without scrollable children; eth target has deliberate min-height:120px (blind fix = regression). Tighten rule first.
[2026-07-28 06:59] ADD (5) SEM-002 x15 findings are FALSE POSITIVES on state-machine pages (accept-invite .state, wsa instructor .slide — h1s in mutually-exclusive display:none containers, one in a11y tree at a time): rule should ignore h1s inside display-toggled containers. ADD (6) SEM-003 x1 residual = forensics/index.html redirect stub (deliberately excluded from h1 batch): rule should skip redirect stubs. ALSO: projects/eye-osint-dashboard.html has 2 VISIBLE h1s (cf-subject template line 741 + page h1 1339) — 1-page manual fix, not batched.
[2026-07-28 07:05] REFINE (5): the state-container SEM-002 exemption must ALSO require exactly ONE .active container per toggle-group in the STATIC markup (Nancy: otherwise the rule swallows a real bug where two states ship .active). REPLACE eye-osint MANUAL note: reclassified as BUG-036 (unescaped code-sample HTML polluting live DOM — escape the sample, do NOT demote headings).
[2026-07-28 14:02] ADD (7) HEUR-034 x298 ROOT CAUSE FOUND: detection regex 'opacity:\s*0(?:\b|[^.\d])' — the \b alternative matches the digit-to-dot boundary in 'opacity: 0.8', so decimal opacities false-match as 0. Fix: replace with lookahead 'opacity:\s*0(?![\d.])'. Sample proof: fifth.html dotPulse (1->0.8->1, never 0) flagged. Expect large FP reduction on refix + rescan. ADD (8) forensics/index.html h1: Nancy PAUSEd the batch-14th edit (reopens a prior exclusion via a DIFFERENT stub subtype precedent; wording should carry 'moved' framing) — DEFERRED as the intentional SEM-003 residual until Frank rules wording.
[2026-07-28 14:40] ADD (9) eduscan-ignore directive parser: reason class [^"']+ silently no-ops the ENTIRE directive when the reason contains an apostrophe (Nancy reproduced: exec() -> null -> shouldIgnore false while the operator believes the issue is exempted). Fix = quote-type-aware capture ("([^"]*)"|'([^']*)'). MUST regression-check the existing live directives (forge-aplus-core1-prep quizzes + dark-arts-ceh-01) when changing the parser.
[2026-07-31 19:05] RE-MEASURED 2026-07-31 against findings.json from today's full scan (12,623 refreshed, 13,078 records). Items (1) and (2) appear ALREADY RESOLVED: TRACK-001 = 0 findings, ENG-002 = 0 findings. Verified these are genuine resolutions, not deleted rules -- both still exist in the validator code (TRACK-001 in parsers/quiz.js, ENG-002 in validators/syntax/engine.js), so the rules still run and find nothing. Item (3) NAV-001/NAV-002 is still live: NAV-001=10, NAV-002=2, and it was always a class RULING not a defect count. So the remaining scope of this ticket is item (3) only. METHOD NOTE: the rule id field in findings.json is .code, NOT .rule/.ruleId -- querying the wrong field returns 0 for everything and reads as 'all resolved'. I hit exactly that on the first pass.
[2026-07-31 21:06] ITEMS 1+2 VERIFIED RESOLVED (re-measured 2026-07-31 against today's full scan): TRACK-001 = 0 findings, ENG-002 = 0 findings, and both rules still exist in the validator source (parsers/quiz.js, validators/syntax/engine.js) so the zeros are genuine resolutions rather than deleted rules. Tool: node _tools/eduscan/recount-classes.js. ITEM 3 (NAV ruling): adjudicated all 12 findings individually, not sampled. My reading is ZERO genuine defects, in 3 classes -- (A) 7 pages that DO have back/home nav the rule's pattern misses (logo-home links on press/partners/vision/products; explicit /index.html on shield/careers; id=homeLink on houses/hub); (B) 1 page whose nav is JS-injected (tenant/instructor.html loads TenantShell.js, whose header says it overrides all Dashboard/Home/Back links); (C) 3-4 immersion-by-design arena sim pages (siem/workstation/broadcast, 0 anchors each) plus a slide deck. WITH NANCY for the class ruling -- I flagged that 'all 12 are false positives' is the conclusion I should be most suspicious of, and asked her to specifically verify a student CAN escape the arena sim pages, since if they cannot that is a real trap and the opposite of a false positive. No rule or page changed.
[2026-07-31 21:13] ITEM 3 PARTIALLY RESOLVED. Nancy PAUSE corrected my classification: 2 of 12 were REAL defects, not false positives -> BUG-075 (P2, tenant/instructor.html strands cold-entry instructors; TenantShell no-ops without stored tenant context) and BUG-076 (P3, admissions deck has zero exit). Validator fix SHIPPED (OpenWorldEngine.js added to navigation.js Pattern 8) -- verified per-file: siem/workstation now clean, the 2 real defects still flagged. STILL OPEN: whether a site-header logo-home link counts as back-navigation for the 6 Class A pages (press, partners, vision, products, shield/careers, houses/hub/index). Nancy raised this as a real question -- the rule may be right and the PAGES may need explicit back-links -- and deliberately did not rule. That is a content-vs-validator call, not mine to make alone. Also still open: distinct exemption rationales needed for arena/broadcast.html (operator kiosk, noindex) and houses/security-plus/index.html (17-line redirect stub, never rendered) -- they must NOT share one blanket rule.
[2026-08-01 02:06] ITEMS 1 AND 2 ARE ALREADY CLOSED -- verified by measurement 2026-07-31, not assumed. This ticket describes them as open gaps; they are not.
(1) TRACK-001 / dark-arts-ceh-01.quiz: handled via an eduscan-ignore directive at line 2 of the quiz carrying the full BUG-007 reasoning, with shouldIgnore() support in parsers/quiz.js:350. Measured with the CORRECT signature parse(content, filePath): TRACK-001 issues=0, ignored=1. The ignored=1 is the part that matters -- it proves the rule SAW the condition and deliberately suppressed it, rather than the rule silently failing to fire. My first attempt passed an object instead of (content, path) and reported ignored=0, which would have looked like a broken exemption.
(2) ENG-002 comment/prose false positive: a comment guard is implemented in validators/syntax/engine.js:512 with a test at tests/run.js:669 that passes and covers three cases -- prose in comments exempt, a real call after a regex literal containing an escaped double-slash still flagged (Nancy's masking case, /https?:\/\// exists in 117 live files), and a keyword-prefixed regex literal still flagged (Chris's HED.js:68 catch). Measured against the file the ticket names: ENG-002 hits on _app/houses/observatory/index.html = 0.
REMAINING SCOPE OF #228 IS ITEM 3 ONLY: the NAV-001/NAV-002 class ruling (arena sim inner pages are immersion-by-design; no universal dashboard-link standard exists, forge lacks one too). That is a deliberate OPERATOR/Nancy decision, not an implementation gap -- Nancy previously declined to rule it. Nothing to build here without that ruling.
[2026-08-02 17:19] [2026-08-02] ITEMS 1 AND 2 ARE ALREADY DONE -- verified by measurement, not rebuilt. The note was stale and would have sent someone to redo finished work.
(1) TRACK-001 false positive on dark-arts-ceh-01.quiz: RESOLVED. The exemption mechanism exists (shouldIgnore + eduscan-ignore directive, parsers/quiz.js:348) and the quiz carries it at line 2 with a full reason citing BUG-007. Ran the parser directly: TRACK-001 REPORTED=0, IGNORED=1 with reason 'trackProgress:false is the BUG-007 double-XP fix...'. Exactly the comment-annotation exemption this task asked for.
(2) ENG-002 matching 'moment' in comments/UI strings: RESOLVED. The comment guard is in validators/syntax/engine.js and has a THREE-fixture test in tests/run.js:669-690 covering prose (must not flag), a real call adjacent to a /https?:\/\// regex literal (must flag -- Nancy's reproduced masking case, 117 live files), and Chris's keyword-prefixed regex idiom from HED.js:68 (must flag). Full suite: 77/77 passed, 0 failed, including '✓ ENG-002 precision'.
(3) NAV-001/NAV-002 class ruling: STILL OPEN and it is a DECISION, not code. Arena sim inner pages (siem/workstation) are immersion-by-design and forge has no dashboard link either, so there is no universal standard to validate against. Needs an operator/curriculum ruling on whether such a standard should exist before the rule can be scoped. Nothing for me to build until that lands.
NET: this task is code-complete. Only the item-3 ruling remains.
